n: Mormon introduces Amulek’s sermon to the people of Ammonihah.
Amulek establishes his identity through his ancestry, reaching back to Aminadi, who interpreted writing on a temple wall written by God’s finger — an event otherwise unrecorded.

f.w: the writing which was upon the wall
f.g: Compare Daniel interpreting the writing on Belshazzar’s wall.

n: Amulek traces his line to Nephi and Lehi, and through Lehi to Manasseh, son of Joseph who was sold into Egypt. He is a true Nephite, a fellow citizen they cannot dismiss.
Amulek is well known, well connected, and wealthy through hard work — a respected local, not an outsider.

f.g: A man of good standing in the community.

n: He first says he never knew much of the Lord’s ways, then corrects himself: he had seen plenty of God’s power, especially in preserving the people.

f.g: An honest self-correction that shows Amulek’s sincerity.

n: He confesses he hardened his heart: called many times, he would not listen — he “knew” yet would not know — until a specific day: the fourth day of the seventh month of the tenth year.

f.w: I was called many times and I would not hear

n: While traveling to visit a relative, an angel told Amulek to go home, for he would feed a hungry, fasting prophet who would bless his household.

f.w: thou shalt feed a prophet of the Lord

n: Amulek obeyed and met the very man the angel described — Alma, who had just been speaking to them.

f.w: I obeyed the voice of the angel
f.g: Amulek’s simple obedience changed his life.

n: Amulek knows Alma is holy because an angel said so.
He also knows Alma’s teachings are true, for the Lord sent his angel to confirm them while Alma lived in his home.

f.g: A solemn oath formula in Hebrew tradition.

n: Alma blessed his whole household and extended family, and the Lord’s blessing rested on them as promised.

f.w: the blessing of the Lord hath rested upon us

n: The people are astonished: now there are two witnesses testifying of their sins and future events.
Some plan to question the missionaries cleverly to trap them into saying something that could be used to convict them.
These were lawyers, hired or appointed by the people to handle legal trials before the judges.
These lawyers were skilled in every trick and clever argument, which made them effective at their profession.
They questioned Amulek, hoping to make him contradict himself.
Amulek perceives their thoughts and calls them hypocrites laying traps for God’s holy servants — the devil’s groundwork.
Their plotting to twist the ways of the righteous will bring down God’s wrath and destroy the people.

f.w: pervert the ways of the righteous

n: Amulek recalls King Mosiah’s warning: when the people’s voice chooses wickedness, they are ripe for destruction.

f.w: if the time should come that the voice of this people should choose iniquity

n: The Lord judges rightly, calling through angels: repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.

f.w: by the voice of his angels

n: The Lord promises to come among his people with fairness and justice in his hands.
Only the prayers of the righteous are keeping the city from destruction — not by a flood as in Noah’s day, but by famine, disease, and war.
If they drive out the righteous, nothing will hold back God’s hand — which is exactly what happens in Alma 14 and 16.

f.w: if ye will cast out the righteous

n: The crowd grows angrier, accusing Amulek of insulting their just laws and wise lawyers.

f.g: Twisting his words to charge him with a crime.

n: Amulek raises his hand and cries louder: why has Satan such a grip that you are blind to truth?

f.w: why hath Satan got such great hold upon your hearts

n: He clarifies: he hasn’t spoken against their law, but in favor of it — and the law itself condemns them.

f.w: I have spoken in favor of your law, to your condemnation
f.g: Their own corrupt lawyers and judges were violating the just law of Mosiah.

n: The foundation of the people’s destruction is being laid by their corrupt lawyers and judges.
The crowd calls him a liar and child of the devil, claiming he spoke against their law and then denied it.

f.g: They hurl back the very charge Alma had earlier made against the wicked.

n: They add that he insulted their lawyers and judges.
The lawyers urge the people to remember these words as evidence against him.

f.g: Gathering testimony for a future trial.

n: The lead accuser is Zeezrom, one of the most skilled lawyers, with a busy practice.
The lawyers’ motive: money. They earned fees from the cases they handled, so stirring up lawsuits paid them.
